name: Trischettn Duel
summary: A two-player, no-trump trick-taking duel over 2 deals of 16 tricks with a talon draw, where pips from won cards and the last trick decide the winner.

player.meaning: The player's private hand of cards, each written like 'Ace of Bells'.
Pips won so far in the current deal, including the last-trick bonus.
Sum of deal pips from completed deals. This is the score.

game.initial: all 32 cards: Ten, Nine, Ace, King, Ober, Unter, Eight, Seven of each of Hearts, Bells, Leaves, Acorns
game.meaning: The full deck. It is rebuilt and shuffled at the start of each deal.
The face-down talon cards below the talon-up card, in order.
The face-up top card of the talon, or 'none'.
Number of cards left in the talon, counting the talon-up card.
The current deal, 1 or 2. It is set to 3 when the match is over.
The current trick within the deal, from 1 to 16.
The seat that leads the current trick.
The card led to the current trick, or 'none'.
The card played by the follower to the current trick, or 'none'.
The seat that won the last trick.

setup: Seat 1 is Player A and seat 2 is Player B.
Both players start with match_total 0 and deal_pips 0.
deal_number is set to 1 and trick_number to 1. The deal itself happens in the first round step, because it also runs at the start of deal 2.

round.effect: When trick_number = 1: rebuild deck with all 32 cards, empty every hand, then draw 8 cards at random from deck into each player's hand. Move the remaining 16 cards into talon in random order, then remove the first talon card and set it as talon_up. Set talon_count = 16, set each deal_pips = 0, and set leader_seat = 1 if deal_number = 1, else 2. Announce the deal number, talon_up and the leader.
Each player sees their own hand plus all public attributes: deal_number, trick_number, leader_seat, led_card, follow_card, talon_up, talon_count, every deal_pips and every match_total.
Remove the chosen card from the leader's hand and set led_card to it. Announce led_card.

round.who: the seat not equal to leader_seat
round.answer: one card from their hand of the suit of led_card; if they hold no card of that suit, any card in their hand
round.effect: Remove the chosen card from the follower's hand and set follow_card to it. Announce follow_card.

If follow_card has the same suit as led_card and its strength is higher (Ten 8, Nine 7, Ace 6, King 5, Ober 4, Unter 3, Eight 2, Seven 1), set trick_winner_seat to the follower's seat; otherwise set it to leader_seat. Add the pips of led_card and follow_card (Ace 3; Ten, Nine, King, Ober, Unter 1; Eight, Seven 0) to the winner's deal_pips, plus 3 if trick_number = 16. Announce the winner and both deal_pips.

When talon_count > 0: append talon_up to the winner's hand and announce which card it was. Remove the first card of talon and append it to the loser's hand, without announcing it. Set talon_count = talon_count - 2. If talon_count > 0, remove the first card of talon and set talon_up to it; otherwise set talon_up = 'none'. Announce talon_up and talon_count.

Set leader_seat = trick_winner_seat, led_card = 'none' and follow_card = 'none'. If trick_number = 16, add each player's deal_pips to their match_total, announce both match_total values, set deal_number = deal_number + 1 and trick_number = 1. Otherwise set trick_number = trick_number + 1.
End the game if deal_number > 2; otherwise continue with the next round.

ending.decided_by: Each player's standing is their match total, the pips summed over both deals (70 available). The higher total wins. Equal totals (35 each) share the win, which is a draw.

rules.text: When the match starts, then there are 2 deals of 16 tricks each, 32 rounds in all, and each round is one trick.
When a deal starts (trick 1 of deal 1 or deal 2), then all 32 cards are shuffled, each player's hand gets 8 cards, and the other 16 form the talon.
When a deal starts, then the top talon card is turned face up as talon_up, talon_count is 16, and both deal_pips are set to 0.
When deal 1 starts, then seat 1 (Player A) leads trick 1; when deal 2 starts, then seat 2 (Player B) leads trick 1.
When a trick begins, then the leader may play any one card from their hand, which is removed from the hand and shown as led_card.
When the follower holds at least one card of the led suit, then only cards of that suit are offered to them.
When the follower holds no card of the led suit, then every card in their hand is offered.
When both cards are of the led suit, then the card of higher strength wins, with Ten 8, Nine 7, Ace 6, King 5, Ober 4, Unter 3, Eight 2, Seven 1.
When the follower's card is not of the led suit, then the leader wins the trick, because there are no trumps.
When a trick is won, then the winner adds the pips of both cards to their deal_pips: Ace 3; Ten, Nine, King, Ober and Unter 1; Eight and Seven 0.
When trick 16 of a deal is won, then the winner adds 3 extra pips to their deal_pips.
When a trick ends and talon_count > 0, then the winner takes talon_up into their hand openly and the loser takes the next talon card into their hand unseen by the winner.
When a talon draw leaves cards in the talon, then the new top card becomes talon_up; when it leaves none, then talon_up becomes 'none'.
When 8 tricks of a deal have been played, then the talon is empty (talon_count 0) and tricks 9 to 16 are played with no drawing.
When a trick ends, then its winner leads the next trick.
When trick 16 of a deal ends, then each player's deal_pips are added to their match_total.
When a deal is scored, then the deal_pips of the two players total 35.
When round 32 ends (deal_number becomes 3), then the game ends and the higher match_total wins.
When both match totals are equal (35 each), then the match is a draw and both players share the win.

When a player looks at the game, then they see only their own hand, but both players see the deal and trick numbers, leader, led_card, follow_card, talon_up, talon_count, both deal_pips and both match totals.

offers.question: Leader plays a card
offers.options: every card in that seat's hand

offers.question: Follower plays a card
offers.who: the seat not equal to leader_seat
offers.options: if the hand holds any card of led_card's suit: only those cards; otherwise every card in the hand

choices.why: The designer set 2. The game is a duel: one leader and one follower per trick, with a talon split between winner and loser. A third player would break the follow-and-draw structure.

choices.what: Card names written as text like 'Ace of Bells', with strength and pips taken from the parameter table
choices.why: The engine has no card type. Strength and pip values are listed as parameters so the trick and scoring arithmetic is explicit.
The rules ask for 'the number of cards left in the talon' to be public. Counting the face-up card makes it 16 at the start and 0 after 8 tricks.
The rules have no table talk. In a two-player zero-sum duel, talk would add words without a real decision about whether to trust a proposal.

A thoughtful player tracks played cards and openly drawn talon cards, decides when to win a trick for talon_up versus duck to save strong cards, keeps Aces (3 pips) safe, and plans the endgame for the 3-pip last trick.

simplifications.what: The deal is run as conditional updates inside the round steps (when trick_number = 1) instead of as separate deal phases
simplifications.why: The step list is flat. A single step with an arithmetic 'when' condition reproduces the start of deal 1 and deal 2.

simplifications.what: The talon-up card taken by the winner goes into their ally-visible hand, and is only announced publicly at the moment it is taken
simplifications.why: The engine has no per-card visibility inside a list. The card was already public as talon_up, so players keep the same knowledge the rules give them.
